Exercise: Romanian Deadlift

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- unilateral_hip_extension
- spinal_flexion

Primary Muscles:

- hamstrings

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- glutes
- lower back

Equipment:

- barbell

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate to high

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:

- spinal_flexibility_and_core_stability
- hamstring_strength_and_hypertrophy
- glute_activation_and_development

Contraindications:

- Lower back pain (unless cleared by a healthcare professional)
- Recent knee surgery

Exercise Variations:

- name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift, equipment: barbell or dumbbell
- name: Romanian Deadlift with Barbell Rollout, equipment: barbell and stability ball

Substitution Options:

- name: Sumo Deadlift High Pull, equipment: barbell
- name: Good Morning, equipment: dumbbells or barbell

Instructions:

- Put a barbell in front of you on the ground and grab it using a pronated (palms facing down) grip that a little wider than shoulder width. Tip: Depending on the weight used, you may need wrist wraps to perform the exercise and also a raised platform in order to allow for better range of motion.
- Bend the knees slightly and keep the shins vertical, hips back and back straight. This will be your starting position.
- Keeping your back and arms completely straight at all times, use your hips to lift the bar as you exhale. Tip: The movement should not be fast but steady and under control.
- Once you are standing completely straight up, lower the bar by pushing the hips back, only slightly bending the knees, unlike when squatting. Tip: Take a deep breath at the start of the movement and keep your chest up. Hold your breath as you lower and exhale as you complete the movement.
- Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
